summary: E2E tested the new Wayly mobile (Expo) surface against the shared backend as cathy@example.com. Backend endpoints for mobile all pass except a response-shape mismatch on /api/participants. Core mobile flows (login, dashboard, statements list+detail, invoices list+detail, Ask Wayly chat, upload screen, settings/plan, more menu + logout) all render and route correctly. One CRITICAL parity bug: mobile ParticipantContext reads res.participants but backend returns {items:[...]}, so cathy's 3 real participants are dropped -> household-fallback shown in switcher, /participants screen says 'No participants added yet', and no X-Participant-Id header is ever set. Two review-request testIDs (settings-manage-plan, more-logout) do not match the code (actual: manage-plan-button, logout-button) - documentation drift only, buttons work.

ui_bugs.issue: Mobile reads res.participants from /api/participants, but the shared backend returns {items:[...]}. Consequently cathy (who has 3 seeded participants) shows 0 participants in-app; switcher only exposes the household fallback and /participants screen shows the empty-state 'No participants added yet'. Reference: /app/mobile/src/context/ParticipantContext.tsx:41-42

Because the participants list is always empty (see above), activeId stays '' and no X-Participant-Id header is ever attached. Any participant-scoped endpoint on mobile is effectively household-scoped. Reference: /app/mobile/src/context/ParticipantContext.tsx:46-48, /app/mobile/src/lib/api.ts:82-84

react_native_issues.issue: Console warns: 'shadow* style props are deprecated. Use boxShadow' and 'props.pointerEvents is deprecated. Use style.pointerEvents'. Non-blocking but will break on future RN Web majors. Coming from theme card shadows / Pressable usage.

parity_issues.issue: Web reads the same /api/participants correctly (uses items[]). Mobile drops the payload because it expects a 'participants' key.
parity_issues.expected: 3 participants visible for cathy on both surfaces
parity_issues.actual: 0 participants on mobile; household fallback only

action_items: FIX: In /app/mobile/src/context/ParticipantContext.tsx change `apiFetch<{ participants: Participant[] }>('/participants')` and `res?.participants` to read from `items` (the shared backend contract) -- e.g. `const res = await apiFetch<{ items: Participant[] }>('/participants'); const list = res?.items || res?.participants || [];`. This immediately restores the switcher, /participants screen, and X-Participant-Id header.

RECONCILE testIDs: review request mentions `settings-manage-plan` and `more-logout` but code uses `manage-plan-button` and `logout-button`. Pick one convention and align the PRD/testIDs so future testing scripts don't drift.
OPTIONAL cleanup: silence react-native-web deprecation warnings (shadow* / pointerEvents) by using boxShadow / style.pointerEvents where possible.
critical_code_review_comments: ParticipantContext.tsx response shape assumption diverges from the shared backend contract (items vs participants) -- validate all shared endpoints against the web client (which is the source of truth) to catch similar drift on other endpoints.

AuthContext signup() hardcodes plan:'free' even though the Wayly product removed the free plan in Dec 2026 (see /app/memory/test_credentials.md). New mobile signups will land as free-plan users, then likely hit the 402 paywall. Should either default to 'family' or accept a plan param and route through the same signup flow as web.

loginWithGoogle for the Expo web preview does a full-page redirect via window.location.href -- OK for the preview, but note that the session_id post-redirect handler in the same file uses extractSessionId(window.location.href) which will fire on ANY /?session_id=... URL, even accidental ones. Consider clearing/validating scope.

success_rate.backend: 90% (9/10 asserts pass; the 10th documents the shape bug)
success_rate.frontend: 88% (11/12 screens verified; participants/switcher blocked by the shape bug)

context_for_next_testing_agent: After the participants fix, re-run test_mobile_backend_flows.py (adjust the participants assertion to expect res['items']) and re-hit /participants + participant-switcher in the mobile UI to confirm the 3 participants appear and that X-Participant-Id is now sent on subsequent calls (inspect network in devtools).
rca of the issue: RCA: /api/participants returns {items: [...]} (verified against production backend for cathy@example.com). The mobile ParticipantContext (line 41) types the response as {participants: Participant[]} and destructures res?.participants, which is always undefined. Fallback resolves to []. Downstream effects: (a) UI shows household-only fallback in switcher, (b) /participants screen renders empty state, (c) activeId never resolves so X-Participant-Id header is never attached to any request. Fix is a 2-line change in ParticipantContext.tsx to read `res.items`.
